title: LEAP 2026
shortDescription: LEAP returns to the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre in Malham from 31 August to 3 September 2026 for its fifth edition, under the theme “Into New Worlds”, with organisers projecting more than 201,000 visitors, 1,800 tech brands, 600 startups, 1,900 investors and over 1,000 speakers across 14-plus stages.
description:
LEAP is Saudi Arabia's flagship technology exhibition and conference, and by attendance the largest technology event in the Middle East. It was launched in 2022 by Tahaluf, the Saudi-headquartered events company created as a joint venture between Informa PLC and the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP), with the Events Investment Fund later taking a stake. The 2026 edition is the fifth, and runs from 31 August to 3 September 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre (RECC) in Malham, north of the capital. Show hours for visitors are 12:00 to 21:00 daily.

The 2026 dates are not the ones originally published. LEAP 5 was first announced for 13–16 April 2026, and the organisers subsequently moved it to the 31 August – 3 September slot. Annabelle Mander, Executive Vice President at Tahaluf and a co-creator of LEAP, framed the change as protecting international participation, saying that hosting LEAP 2026 through early September "ensures we continue to deliver the global participation and world-class experience that our community expects". Some listings and aggregator sites still carry the April dates, and a number of them also misname the venue as Riyadh Front; the official site lists RECC Malham.

Scale is the defining characteristic. Organisers project more than 201,000 visitors for 2026, alongside over 1,800 global technology brands, 600 startups, 1,900 investors and more than 1,000 speakers programmed across 20-plus stages. The content spans artificial intelligence, cloud and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, fintech, health technology, smart cities, climate and energy technology, space, gaming, sports technology and digital commerce. The exhibition floor draws the hyperscalers and large enterprise vendors — Google Cloud, Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, Huawei, Dell Technologies, SAP, Salesforce, Ericsson, AMD, Qualcomm, Lenovo, HP, Foxconn and Cerebras among them — alongside Saudi national champions including stc, Aramco, Elm, Alat and HUMAIN.

What gives LEAP its weight in the region is that it has become the venue where Saudi technology investment is announced. The 2025 edition opened with a record US$14.9 billion of new AI investment commitments, including Salesforce (US$500 million for Hyperforce), Databricks (US$300 million), Tencent Cloud (US$150 million), SambaNova (US$140 million) and a KKR–Gulf Data Hub data-centre partnership of up to 300 megawatts. The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology put cumulative technology infrastructure investment announced at LEAP since 2022 at more than US$42.4 billion, and organisers reported a US$820 million economic impact for Riyadh from the 2025 edition alone.

For founders and investors, LEAP runs a substantial startup and capital programme rather than a token pitch corner. The Rocket Fuel Pitch Competition returns for a fifth edition with 100 selected startups competing for a US$1 million equity-free prize fund across several award categories. Startups can take a Startup Pod (exhibition stand plus automatic Rocket Fuel eligibility and coaching workshops) or a Founder Pass (individual attendance with AI-assisted investor matchmaking and Ecosystem Xchange sessions). The 2026 edition also brings a new GameX Creative zone built with Savvy Games Group, ESL FACEIT Group, Steer Studios, MDLBeast, Red Sea Film Foundation and Kojima Productions, and an expanded Sports Tech Hub involving the English FA, LaLiga, the Saudi Pro League, Juventus, Atlético Madrid, Tottenham Hotspur, Ferrari and the Aston Martin Formula One team. DeepFest, the dedicated AI event powered by SDAIA, is co-located on the same site and dates.

whatToExpect.detail: More than 1,800 technology brands across multiple halls, from hyperscalers and chipmakers to Saudi national operators and sovereign-backed AI ventures.
Over 1,000 speakers programmed across thematic stages covering AI, fintech, health tech, climate and energy, space, smart cities, gaming and sports technology.

whatToExpect.lead: Investment announcements you will read about later
whatToExpect.detail: LEAP is where Saudi technology infrastructure and AI commitments are typically unveiled; the 2025 opening day alone carried US$14.9 billion of new investment.

whatToExpect.lead: A serious startup and investor programme
whatToExpect.detail: The Rocket Fuel Pitch Competition puts 100 startups in front of judges for a US$1 million equity-free prize fund, alongside structured investor matchmaking.
The co-located AI event powered by SDAIA runs inside the same footprint, and LEAP passes include access to DeepFest conference stages.
GameX Creative debuts as a gaming, esports and digital content zone, while the Sports Tech Hub returns at larger scale with clubs, leagues and motorsport teams.
Roughly three-quarters of the 1,900 investors at the 2025 edition travelled from outside Saudi Arabia, and the exhibitor base is similarly global.
Doors open to visitors at 12:00 and the halls stay open until 21:00 each day, so the schedule leans into afternoon and evening networking.

venueAddress: Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre, Malham, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia
organizerDescription: Tahaluf (Arabic for 'alliance') is a Saudi-headquartered large-scale live events company founded in 2022 as a joint venture between Informa PLC and the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP). The Events Investment Fund, part of Saudi Arabia's National Development Fund, later acquired a stake. Tahaluf builds internationally benchmarked B2B platforms across technology, real estate, cybersecurity, healthcare and fintech in support of Vision 2030, and its portfolio includes LEAP, DeepFest and LEAP East in Hong Kong.
figuresNote: All figures above are organiser projections for the 2026 edition, published in the LEAP 5 announcement and carried by The Fintech Times, entARABI and the syndicated press release. For context, the completed 2025 edition reported 200,000 attendees, more than 1,800 exhibiting tech brands (830 of them first-time exhibitors), 680 startups, 1,900 investors of whom 74% travelled from overseas, and over 1,000 speakers. LEAP 2025 opened with US$14.9 billion of new AI investment announcements and closed with a reported US$820 million economic impact for Riyadh. Country count is not published by the organisers, so it is left null rather than estimated. Organisers also publish 14+ stages, 20+ tracks and state that 69% of speakers are international.

speakers.name: Matt Garman
speakers.title: Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Matt Garman became CEO of Amazon Web Services in June 2024, having joined Amazon as an intern in 2005 and spent much of his career building the EC2 compute business. He previously led AWS sales, marketing and global services. AWS is a long-standing LEAP exhibitor and has been central to Saudi cloud region and AI infrastructure commitments announced at the event.

speakers.name: Justin Hotard
speakers.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Justin Hotard took over as President and CEO of Nokia in April 2025, arriving from Intel where he ran the Data Center and AI group, and before that from HPE where he led high-performance computing and AI. At Nokia he has pushed the company further towards AI and data-centre networking alongside its telecoms business.

speakers.name: Tareq Amin
speakers.title: Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Tareq Amin leads HUMAIN, the Saudi artificial intelligence company launched under the Public Investment Fund to build the Kingdom's AI infrastructure, data centres and Arabic-language models. He previously served as CEO of Aramco Digital and, before that, as CEO of Rakuten Symphony and CTO of Rakuten Mobile, where he built one of the first fully cloud-native mobile networks.

speakers.name: Andrew Feldman
speakers.title: Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Andrew Feldman co-founded Cerebras Systems in 2015 and has led its development of wafer-scale processors designed for large-model training and high-throughput inference. He previously co-founded SeaMicro, the low-power server company acquired by AMD in 2012. Cerebras has partnered on AI compute build-outs in the Gulf and is also listed among DeepFest 2026 exhibitors and speakers.

speakers.name: Hanne Jesca Bax
speakers.title: Global Vice Chair, Clients & Industries
speakers.bio: Hanne Jesca Bax is EY's Global Vice Chair for Clients & Industries, a role in which she oversees the firm's relationships with C-suite buyers and its solutions innovation agenda, and acts as global sponsor for the SAP and ServiceNow alliances. She has been with EY since 1996 and previously served as Managing Partner Markets for the Netherlands and Belgium and as EMEIA Markets and Accounts Leader.

speakers.name: Chandra Donelson
speakers.title: Data and AI strategist; former Chief Data and AI Officer, United States Space Force
speakers.bio: Chandra Donelson served as the first permanent Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the United States Space Force, appointed in 2023, where she oversaw data, AI and software integration and led the service's adoption of generative AI. She announced her departure from the role in April 2026 and now works as an independent data and AI strategist and author. She was announced for LEAP in the February 2026 lineup while still in the Space Force post; the later DeepFest announcement describes her by her post-government title.

speakers.name: Lisa Su
speakers.title: Chair and Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Lisa Su has been chief executive of AMD since 2014 and became chair of the board in 2022. Under her leadership AMD moved into high-performance computing and AI accelerators, and she was named to the LEAP 2026 headline lineup as Saudi Arabia marks 2026 as its Year of Artificial Intelligence.

speakers.name: Michio Kaku

speakers.bio: Michio Kaku is a theoretical physicist, co-founder of string field theory and a widely published science communicator. He appears on the LEAP 2026 speaker roster.

faqs.question: When and where does LEAP 2026 take place?
faqs.answer: LEAP 2026 runs from Monday 31 August to Thursday 3 September 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre (RECC) in Malham, north of Riyadh. Halls are open to visitors from 12:00 to 21:00 each day; exhibitors have earlier access from 09:00.

faqs.question: Didn't LEAP 2026 used to be in April?
faqs.answer: Yes. The fifth edition was originally announced for 13–16 April 2026 and was later rescheduled by the organisers to 31 August – 3 September 2026. Tahaluf framed the move as preserving global participation. Several third-party listing sites still show the April dates, so use the official site as the reference.

faqs.question: How much does a pass cost?
faqs.answer: LEAP sells a tiered range of passes — General Admission, Priority, VIP, Founder, Investor and Student — plus free accreditation for verified press. Pricing changes between phases and is not fixed across the cycle, so check the official 2026 ticket page for current rates. Tickets are non-refundable.

faqs.question: Do international attendees need a visa for Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: Most international visitors need a visa. Citizens of more than 60 countries are eligible for the Saudi tourist e-visa, which is typically valid for one year with multiple entries and stays of up to 90 days, and travellers holding a valid, previously used US, UK or Schengen visa or permanent residency may also qualify. Apply through the official Saudi eVisa portal and check current eligibility well before travelling.

faqs.question: Is DeepFest included with a LEAP pass?
faqs.answer: DeepFest is co-located with LEAP at the same venue on the same dates, and LEAP conference passes include access to DeepFest stages and the DeepFest exhibition. Student and press passes are explicitly described as covering conference access across both LEAP and DeepFest stages.

faqs.question: How do I get to the venue, and is there parking?
faqs.answer: RECC Malham sits north of central Riyadh, roughly 15 minutes by road from King Khalid International Airport. The venue has more than 7,500 parking spaces, and on-site parking is allocated to Priority, VIP, Founder and Investor pass holders. Public transport to the site is limited, so most attendees arrive by car, taxi or ride-hailing apps such as Uber and Careem; shuttle buses also operate on show days.

faqs.question: Is LEAP worth it for an early-stage startup?
faqs.answer: It is built for that audience. Startups can take a Startup Pod, which includes an exhibition stand, coaching workshops and automatic eligibility for the Rocket Fuel Pitch Competition — 100 companies competing for a US$1 million equity-free prize fund. Founders attending without a stand can take a Founder Pass for investor matchmaking and Ecosystem Xchange sessions. Organisers project more than 1,900 investors on site.

faqs.question: What is the dress code?
faqs.answer: Business casual is recommended. National dress is also welcome and commonly worn in Saudi Arabia. Comfortable footwear is worth it — the halls involve a lot of walking — and a light layer helps in the air-conditioned indoor spaces.

faqs.question: What are the show hours?
faqs.answer: Halls are open to visitors from 12:00 to 21:00 each day, 31 August to 3 September 2026. Exhibitors get earlier access, 09:00 to 21:30 daily, to prepare and break down their stands.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum age?
faqs.answer: Yes — LEAP is an 18+ event.

faqs.question: What is the theme of LEAP 2026?
faqs.answer: “Into New Worlds”. Tahaluf chief executive Mike Champion framed the fifth edition as taking LEAP's ambition “into new worlds, unlocking investment and shaping the technologies that will define the next decade”, with Saudi Arabia marking 2026 as its Year of Artificial Intelligence.

faqs.question: How many stages and tracks are there?
faqs.answer: Organisers publish 14+ stages and 20+ tracks for 2026, including the Main Stage, the Orbital Tracks (sector programmes covering fintech, health tech, climate tech, space, gaming, sports tech, smart cities, retail, edutech, 4IR and the creative economy), the CODE Stage for digital entrepreneurship, the Rocket Fuel startup pitch stage and the co-located DeepFest programme.

sideEvents.description: DeepFest returns for its fourth edition, powered by the Saudi Authority for Data and Artificial Intelligence (SDAIA) and organised by Tahaluf. It runs alongside LEAP at the same venue and on the same dates as the region's dedicated AI event, with companies including EY, Snowflake, Alteryx and Xerox showing applied AI use cases and live demos in the Tech Arena.

The strongest startup across the competition takes the US$250,000 LEAP Award. Rounds run through the show on the Rocket Fuel Stage, from semi-finals to the pitch finale.

title: DeepFest 2026
tagline: Saudi Arabia's dedicated AI event, in the Kingdom's Year of Artificial Intelligence
shortDescription: DeepFest, the AI and deep technology event powered by SDAIA and co-located with LEAP, returns to Riyadh from 31 August to 3 September 2026 with 180-plus speakers and more than 120 exhibitors, in the year Saudi Arabia has designated its Year of Artificial Intelligence.
description:
DeepFest is Saudi Arabia's dedicated artificial intelligence and deep technology event. It launched in 2023 as a co-located platform inside LEAP, is organised by Tahaluf and is powered by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA). The 2026 edition — its fourth — runs from 31 August to 3 September 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre (RECC) in Malham, sharing the venue, the dates and much of the audience with LEAP.

The framing for 2026 is national. Saudi Arabia has designated 2026 its Year of Artificial Intelligence, an initiative backed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in his capacity as Prime Minister and Chairman of SDAIA, and the organisers position DeepFest as the principal venue where that state agenda meets the international AI ecosystem. That gives the event a different character from LEAP's broad technology floor: it is narrower, more technical, and more closely tied to policy and sovereign infrastructure questions.

The 2026 programme spans the AI stack rather than a single layer of it — AI governance and ethics, sovereign compute and infrastructure, autonomous systems and robotics, security and sustainability — alongside applied deployment across healthcare, supply chains, media and the creator economy. Format is a mix of conference talks, technical deep dives, workshops and live demonstrations; organisers have flagged real-time deepfake detection and AI-generated music performances among the demos, and a curated exhibition floor of AI companies rather than a general technology hall.

Organisers list more than 180 speakers and over 120 exhibitors for 2026, with first-time exhibitors and sponsors including Google Cloud, AMD, Salesforce, EY, Cerebras, Supermicro, Blaize and Xerox. The attendance figure quoted for DeepFest, 68,000-plus, is drawn from the 2025 edition; the event has grown steadily from roughly 20,000 attendees at its 2023 debut to 48,000 in 2024 and 68,000 in 2025. Because DeepFest sits inside the LEAP footprint, it also has access to LEAP's investor and startup programmes, which for 2026 project more than 600 startups and 1,900 investors on site.

For the region's AI community, DeepFest is the annual point where national programmes, enterprise buyers and researchers are in the same building. Saudi Arabia's AI build-out — SDAIA's national strategy, the PIF-backed national AI company HUMAIN, large-scale data-centre and compute commitments, and partnerships with global chipmakers and model developers — has moved fast enough that the practical questions have shifted from strategy to deployment, procurement and governance. That is the conversation DeepFest is built around.

whatToExpect.detail: More than 120 exhibitors focused specifically on artificial intelligence, including first-time participants Google Cloud, AMD, Salesforce, EY, Cerebras, Supermicro, Blaize and Xerox.
The programme mixes conference talks with technical deep dives, hands-on workshops and live demonstrations across four days.

whatToExpect.lead: Governance and sovereignty on the agenda
whatToExpect.detail: Sessions cover AI governance, ethics, security, sustainability and sovereign infrastructure alongside the commercial applications.
Demos announced for 2026 include real-time deepfake detection and AI-generated music performance, putting the technology itself on stage.

whatToExpect.lead: The national AI agenda in the room
whatToExpect.detail: Powered by SDAIA and staged in Saudi Arabia's designated Year of Artificial Intelligence, with national strategy and real-world deployment as the organising themes.
Deployment tracks span healthcare, supply chains, media and the creator economy rather than treating AI as a standalone category.
DeepFest sits inside the LEAP footprint, so attendees also reach LEAP's exhibition, investor programme and startup zone on the same badge.

speakers.name: Andrew Feldman
speakers.title: Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer
speakers.bio: Andrew Feldman co-founded Cerebras Systems in 2015 and has led its development of wafer-scale processors built for large-model training and high-throughput inference. He previously co-founded SeaMicro, the low-power server company acquired by AMD in 2012. Cerebras is also listed among DeepFest 2026's first-time exhibitors and sponsors.

speakers.name: Michio Kaku
speakers.title: Professor of Theoretical Physics
speakers.bio: Michio Kaku is a theoretical physicist at the City College of New York and one of the co-founders of string field theory. He is among the most widely read science popularisers of his generation, with bestsellers including The Future of Humanity and Quantum Supremacy, and is a regular presence on the international conference circuit.

speakers.name: Joe Atkinson
speakers.title: Global Chief AI Officer
speakers.bio: Joe Atkinson is PwC's Global Chief AI Officer, responsible for the firm's artificial intelligence strategy and its deployment across the global network. He previously served as PwC US Chief Products and Technology Officer and as US Chief Digital Officer, roles in which he led large-scale internal technology transformation.

speakers.name: Luc Dammann
speakers.title: President, EMEA
speakers.bio: Luc Dammann is President of Adobe EMEA, overseeing the company's business across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. He joined Adobe in 2020 from SAP, where he spent much of his career in senior regional leadership roles. Adobe has been a recurring participant at DeepFest since earlier editions.

speakers.name: Chandra Donelson
speakers.title: Data and AI strategist and author; former Chief Data and AI Officer, United States Space Force
speakers.bio: Chandra Donelson was the first permanent Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the United States Space Force, appointed in 2023, where she oversaw data, AI and software integration and led the service's adoption of generative AI tooling. She announced her departure from the role in April 2026. DeepFest lists her as a global data and AI strategist, author and three-time chief data and AI officer.

speakers.name: Jack McCauley
speakers.title: Innovator in Residence and Board Trustee
speakers.bio: Jack McCauley is a hardware engineer and inventor who co-founded Oculus VR and served as its chief engineer, building early Rift prototypes before the company's acquisition by Facebook. He is now Innovator in Residence at UC Berkeley's Jacobs Institute for Design Innovation and sits on the university's board of trustees.

speakers.name: Daniel Bedingfield
speakers.title: Singer, songwriter and record producer
speakers.bio: Daniel Bedingfield is a New Zealand-born British singer, songwriter and producer who topped the UK charts with 'Gotta Get Thru This' and won a Brit Award for British Male Solo Artist in 2004. He appears at DeepFest 2026 in the context of the event's creator-economy and AI-generated music programming.

faqs.question: When and where is DeepFest 2026?
faqs.answer: DeepFest 2026 runs from Monday 31 August to Thursday 3 September 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition & Convention Centre (RECC) in Malham, north of Riyadh. It is co-located with LEAP, sharing the venue, the dates and the visitor show hours of 12:00 to 21:00 daily.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate ticket for DeepFest, or is it included with LEAP?
faqs.answer: DeepFest is accessed on a LEAP pass. LEAP conference passes include access to DeepFest stages and the DeepFest exhibition — student and press passes are explicitly described as covering conference access across both LEAP and DeepFest. Check the official registration page for the current pass structure.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: Pass prices vary by tier and by sales phase and are not published as a fixed figure across the cycle. Verified media receive complimentary press accreditation, and student passes are discounted with a .edu email verification. Check the official LEAP ticket page for current pricing.

faqs.question: Who is DeepFest actually for?
faqs.answer: It is aimed at people working at the sharp end of AI: researchers, ML and data engineers, enterprise AI adopters, founders, investors, and policymakers and regulators. The programme mixes technical deep dives and workshops with governance and strategy sessions, so it is more specialised than LEAP's general technology floor.

faqs.question: Do international attendees need a visa for Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: Most do. Citizens of more than 60 countries can apply for the Saudi tourist e-visa, typically valid for one year with multiple entries and stays of up to 90 days, and holders of a valid, previously used US, UK or Schengen visa or permanent residency may also be eligible. Apply through the official Saudi eVisa portal and confirm current eligibility ahead of travel.

faqs.question: How do I get to the venue?
faqs.answer: RECC Malham is roughly 15 minutes by road from King Khalid International Airport, north of central Riyadh. The venue has more than 7,500 parking spaces, with on-site parking allocated to premium pass holders. Public transport to the site is limited, so most attendees travel by car, taxi or ride-hailing apps such as Uber and Careem.

faqs.question: How large is DeepFest?
faqs.answer: Organisers list more than 180 speakers and over 120 exhibitors for 2026. The 68,000-plus attendance figure widely quoted for DeepFest is the 2025 result, up from around 48,000 in 2024 and 20,000 at the 2023 debut. Because DeepFest sits inside LEAP, the wider site is projected to draw more than 201,000 visitors.

faqs.question: Is there anything for AI startups specifically?
faqs.answer: DeepFest runs inside LEAP's footprint, so AI founders can use LEAP's startup and investor programme — the Startup Pod exhibition package, the Founder Pass with investor matchmaking, and the Rocket Fuel Pitch Competition, where 100 startups compete for a US$1 million equity-free prize fund. Details and eligibility are on the official LEAP startup pages.
